terms.name: Backend
terms.description: A configured LLM service endpoint the gateway can route queries to. May be local (running on the same machine) or cloud (remote API).

terms.name: Backend Pool
terms.description: The in-memory registry of all configured backends and their current availability state, maintained at runtime by the backend-pool component.

terms.name: Query
terms.description: A single request from a developer submitted to the gateway for routing and processing by a backend.

terms.name: Route Decision
terms.description: The output of the routing step: which backend was selected for a given query and the reason for selection, including the assigned complexity tier.

terms.name: Classifier
terms.description: The component that analyses a query and assigns it a complexity tier (simple, moderate, or complex) to inform routing decisions.

terms.name: Router
terms.description: The component that selects a backend for a query based on its complexity tier, configured priority order, and backend availability.

terms.name: Complexity Tier
terms.description: A categorical label assigned to a query by the Classifier indicating how capable a backend needs to be to handle it. Values are simple, moderate, or complex.

terms.name: Fallback
terms.description: The automatic selection of the next available backend when the preferred backend is unavailable or returns an error, triggered by the Router.

terms.name: Log Entry
terms.description: A persisted record of a single processed query including the backend used, routing decision, response latency, and outcome.

terms.name: Routing Overhead
terms.description: The latency added by the gateway's classification and routing logic on top of the backend's own response time, measured in milliseconds.

terms.name: Local Backend
terms.description: A backend running as a process on the same machine as the gateway, accessed via localhost. Examples include llama.cpp, LM Studio, and Ollama.

terms.name: Cloud Backend
terms.description: A backend accessed via a remote HTTP API, typically requiring an API key for authentication. Examples include Anthropic API and OpenRouter.

terms.name: OpenAI-compatible
terms.description: Conforming to the request and response format of the OpenAI Chat Completions API, allowing clients built for OpenAI to work without modification.

terms.name: Priority Order
terms.description: The user-configured ranked list of backends the Router consults in sequence when selecting a backend for a query.

terms.name: Override
terms.description: An explicit instruction from the developer to route a query to a specific backend, bypassing classification and priority logic.
